props.title: Once Upon a Honeymoon
props.initialSlug: Romance blooms amid wartime espionage in Europe

sections.content: Once Upon a Honeymoon represents a fascinating intersection of romantic comedy and wartime propaganda, starring Cary Grant and Ginger Rogers at the height of their careers. The film, directed by Leo McCarey, daringly blends screwball comedy elements with serious anti-Nazi messaging - a rare combination for Hollywood during WWII. It follows Rogers as Katie O'Hara, a former burlesque queen masquerading as a aristocrat who marries a Nazi baron, while Grant plays an American radio reporter trying to expose Nazi activities. The film shares thematic DNA with Ernst Lubitsch's To Be or Not to Be (1942), using humor to address the growing Nazi threat. To Be or Not to Be|1942|Jack Benny and Carole Lombard star in Lubitsch's daring comedy about a Polish theater troupe outsmarting Nazis|HBO Max Foreign Correspondent|1940|Hitchcock's thriller about an American reporter uncovering Nazi conspiracies in Europe|Criterion The Mortal Storm|1940|Margaret Sullavan and James Stewart in a drama about a German family torn apart by Nazi ideology|TCM

The film's uneasy marriage of romantic comedy and war drama reflects Hollywood's struggle to address WWII in its early years. While Mrs. Miniver (1942) took a straight dramatic approach and The Great Dictator (1940) went for outright satire, Once Upon a Honeymoon attempts to walk a tightrope between genres. McCarey, known for sophisticated comedies like The Awful Truth (1937), brings his signature touch to the romantic elements while incorporating unprecedented darker themes for a mainstream Hollywood film of the era.

Rogers and Grant's chemistry elevates material that could have fallen flat in lesser hands. Their previous pairing in In Name Only (1939) helped establish their rapport, though this film pushes them into more complex dramatic territory. The film's structure follows the couple through Vienna, Prague, and Warsaw as Nazi Germany expands, providing a unique perspective on historical events through the lens of romantic comedy conventions. Mrs. Miniver|1942|Oscar-winning drama about an English family's courage during WWII|TCM The Great Dictator|1940|Chaplin's bold satirical attack on Hitler and fascism|Criterion Casablanca|1942|Classic wartime romance starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman|HBO Max SUBHEAD: Wartime Romance in Hollywood

The film's release coincided with a wave of anti-Nazi Hollywood productions following America's entry into WWII. While Casablanca (1942) would become the definitive wartime romance, Once Upon a Honeymoon took bigger risks with its tone and subject matter. The film's treatment of concentration camps and Jewish persecution was unusually direct for its time, though filtered through its romantic comedy framework. This approach shares similarities with The Shop Around the Corner (1940), which set its romance against the backdrop of pre-war Budapest with subtle political undertones.
